I can’t identify the cause of this particular missed run from [B_255](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/feature_descriptions/B_255_scheduled_task_did_not_start.md:15). It records only that a task scheduled for an hour later that day did not start; it gives no schedule ID, selected time, schedule status, or runtime error.

The code converts the entered local time to a timestamp, registers a desktop timer, and re-registers pending timers when the project loads ([time conversion](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/schedule/action_schedule_trigger.ts:10), [timer registration](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/schedule/schedule_timers.js:27), [project startup](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_scheduler_service.js:122)). That trace does not establish why this task was missed. The persisted `.md2-schedules.json` record and an error or run log from the scheduled time are needed to distinguish a timer that never fired from an action that failed to start. I made no file changes.

The persisted .md2-schedules.json record and an error or run log from the scheduled time are needed to distinguish a timer that never fired from an action that failed to start. I made no file changes.

scheduled tasks should be managed by the electron backend. this should have a scheduler service. the react app should only monitor for changes in the electron backend's scheduler
I’ll check where Electron starts the scheduler and how React observes it. The distinction may explain why a persisted task was not armed.

You’re right about the intended ownership. The code already has an Electron [ActionSchedulerService](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_scheduler_service.js:88) that stores schedules and runs the timers. React registers a schedule through the Electron bridge, then refreshes its display ([registration](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_defaults.ts:177)). Its [ActiveScheduleService](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/actions/active_schedule_service.ts:66) reads schedule state for the UI; it does not fire tasks.

I missed an architectural gap in my first answer: **Electron starts the scheduler for a project only when that project is activated through a bridge call**, such as `loadProject` or `loadProjectRoot ([activation](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js:143)). It is not started independently when Electron launches. That could explain a missed task if the project was never activated during that session. Closing the app also stops the scheduler.

The B_255 report still does not say whether Electron was running, whether the project was active, or what status the schedule reached, so I cannot establish that this gap caused this specific incident.
